title: [Decision] Erasure: multi-step to trigger, but irreversible + complete once executed — confirm no recoverable off-chain link survives (incl. backups)
description:
Decision/confirmation for **Stuart** (split out of [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position)). This is the foundation of the whole GDPR Art.17 position, so it needs an explicit sign-off.

## Requirement (Kam)

Erasing a data subject should take **multiple deliberate steps** (guard against accidental deletion), but **once executed it must be gone for good — irreversible and complete.**

## Why it's the crux

Our Art.17 position is "anonymisation by destruction": the permanent on-chain record (a hash + opaque tokens) becomes anonymous because the orphaned token **marries to nothing recoverable by anyone**. That only holds if **every** off-chain link is genuinely destroyed — not just the live DB row, but the M365 source documents, KYC images, search indexes, logs, the PII vault (`vault_entries`), and crucially **immutable backups** (you cannot delete a row from a 7-year immutable backup).

## The mechanism that makes "gone for good" true even in backups

**Crypto-shredding.** All PII is AES-256-GCM encrypted (per-tenant DEKs already exist). On erasure, **destroy the key** → the ciphertext sitting in backups becomes permanently unrecoverable. Today `gdprService.executeErasure` does row anonymise/soft-delete + a `USER_ERASED` fan-out, but does **not** destroy encryption keys — so a backup may still hold recoverable ciphertext. Closing that is what turns "deleted from the live DB" into "gone for good everywhere."

## For Stuart to confirm / decide

1. **Multi-step trigger** — e.g. request → admin approval → typed confirmation. Confirm the controls/UX (no one-click irreversible deletes).
2. **"Gone for good" = key-destruction (crypto-shred) on erasure**, not just row-delete. Confirm we adopt this as the guarantee.
3. **Full-surface coverage** — confirm the destruction reaches every off-chain place a recoverable link could survive: live DB, `vault_entries`, M365 source docs, KYC images, search indexes, application logs, **backups** (via key-destruction). Enumerate + confirm none retains a recoverable link. Anything that does → file as an implementation gap.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Erasure model confirmed: multi-step trigger + irreversible + crypto-shred + full off-chain surface coverage.
- [ ] Residual-link gaps (if any) filed as implementation tickets.

Related: [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position) (DPIA note), tracker [KS-229](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-229/tracker-2026-06-10-platform-assurance-review-gap-analysis-remediation).

nodes.body:
**BLUF — the decision is still open and still Stuart's, but its technical foundation moved: the mechanism this ticket assumes (crypto-shred via per-subject keys) does not exist and is gated on KS-291. Verified 2026-08-12, nothing changed.**

**Recommendation:** don't chase Stuart for a sign-off yet (and he's out sick). The honest sequencing is KS-291 first — a sign-off on "irreversible and complete once executed" is not worth having while the mechanism that would make it true is unbuilt.

**Detail**

1. **The premise correction on this ticket (2026-06-18) still holds:** PII is encrypted with a **single master key** (`encryptedField.ts`'s keyRing is versioned, not per-tenant or per-subject), so there is no per-subject key to destroy. Crypto-shredding as written is not achievable today, and the Art.17 "backup-proof erasure" guarantee rests on it.
2. **That is what makes the decision premature rather than blocked-on-a-person.** The requirement — multiple deliberate steps to trigger, irreversible and complete once executed — is a sound product position, but the second half is currently unenforceable for anything already written to an immutable backup.
3. **What would make it decidable:** KS-291 (DEK envelope, per-subject keys), after which "destroy the key" becomes a real operation and the enumeration on this ticket (M365 sources, KYC images, search indexes, logs, `vault_entries`, backups) becomes checkable one surface at a time. KS-292/293 track the `executeErasure` quirks.

Left open and assigned as-is; no nudge sent.

**Erasure-surface enumeration + key correction (verified against code, 2026-06-18).**

⚠️ **Premise correction:** this ticket says 'per-tenant DEKs already exist' — they don't. PII is encrypted with a **single master key** (`encryptedField.ts` keyRing is by *version*, not tenant/subject). So **crypto-shred as written is not achievable today** — there's no per-subject key to destroy. Split to a dedicated architecture item (see sub-issues). The Art.17 'backup-proof erasure' guarantee depends on building per-subject/per-tenant key envelopes first.

**Verified gaps filed as sub-issues:** (1) crypto-shred infeasible / needs per-subject DEK; (2) dead key-deletion code (non-existent tables); (3) refresh_tokens not deleted.

**Reviewed, NOT a gap:** M365 cascade subscriber deliberately does nothing — `svc_m365_connections` OAuth tokens are **org-scoped, not per-user**; deleting on one user's erasure would break the whole org's connection (documented in `m365-integration/src/userErasedSubscriber.ts`). Correct for per-user Art.17.

**Still to VERIFY before filing (agent-surfaced, not yet code-confirmed by me — flagged so they're not lost):** KYC image blob deletion, fire-and-forget cascade completion guarantee, app-log PII redaction, Redis user.erased event-history purge, DSR-record anonymisation, backup DEK-rotation policy. Will confirm each against code before raising — won't auto-file unverified.

**Multi-step trigger (the other half of the requirement):** not yet assessed — needs a look at the DSR request→approval→confirm UX.
